use_case_summary: Primary workloads: customer support chat (latency-sensitive, many short sessions), embeddings for semantic search across financial docs, reranking for results pipelines, fraud-detection batch scoring
Traffic shape: steady baseline traffic during US market hours 08:00-18:00 ET with sharp spikes at open/close (~2.5-3x), weekday heavy, weekends low
Latency targets: p50 < 75ms, p95 < 250ms for chat short prompts (<=256 tokens). Batch embeddings can tolerate higher latency.
Throughput target: need to sustain ~1k-2k tokens/sec during baseline with ability to absorb peaks to 4k tok/sec for short windows
Model preferences: open models on 7B-13B for chat; LLM + specialist reranker; embeddings with 1024-d vectors; preference for quantized variants if quality preserved
cost_modeling: Objective: show economics for reserved Dedicated capacity (committed GPUs) vs host/spike behavior; provide clear unit cost per token under utilization scenarios

Assumptions used in model (shared): per-GPU fully-burdened monthly cost = $7,000 (includes infra, support, network, slot reservation). GPU baseline peak throughput assumption = 200 tokens/sec per GPU on target model (short-context optimized).
Capacity math (per GPU): 200 tok/sec * 3600 * 24 = 17,280,000 tok/day => ~518,400,000 tok/month (100% utilization).
Operational utilization scenarios: low = 25% (129.6M tok/mo), baseline = 40% (207.36M tok/mo), high = 60% (311.04M tok/mo).
Per-token unit economics (per GPU): at baseline 40% util => 207.36M tok/mo => cost per 1M tokens = $7,000 / 207.36 ≈ $33.75 per 1M tokens (≈ $0.03375 per 1k tokens).
Sensitivity: at 60% util cost per 1M = $7,000 / 311.04 ≈ $22.50 per 1M tokens; at 25% util cost per 1M = $7,000 / 129.6 ≈ $54.01 per 1M tokens.

Commit level scenarios (monthly commit cost): 4 GPUs = $28,000/mo, 8 GPUs = $56,000/mo, 16 GPUs = $112,000/mo. Token capacity at baseline util: 4 GPUs => ~829.44M tok/mo, 8 GPUs => ~1.66B tok/mo, 16 GPUs => ~3.32B tok/mo.
Effective blended unit cost is stable across commit sizes given same utilization (per-GPU math above). Key lever is utilization — higher utilization lowers $/token significantly.

Burst planning: recommend model for spike handling - commit to 8 GPUs for baseline (covers steady demand + headroom), enable burst pool (on-demand or partner burst) to 2x baseline. Include conservative headroom factor 1.5x for peak planning.

Break-even considerations vs hosted: provide host comparisons in separate sheet, but internal rule-of-thumb: if sustained utilization on committed GPUs > ~45-50% over contract term, Dedicated TCO likely favorable versus equivalent hosted list prices for similar performance (dependent on model and token mix).

Operational recommendations: 6-12 month commit window with quarterly utilization reviews; include rollover or true-up credits for under-utilization; allow predefined burst capacity at negotiated incremental rate to avoid SLA violations during market events.

SLA negotiation asks from customer side: guaranteed throughput floor (tokens/sec) for committed GPUs, p95 latency target for short prompts with sample benchmark suite, uptime 99.95% with financial credits, 24/7 critical support with 1h response for Sev1, and SLA cap/penalty tiers.

Risk items noted: traffic forecast uncertainty is largest sensitivity (spike magnitude and weekday concentration). Recommendation: start with 8 GPU commit + 2-month runway to gather real telemetry, then scale to 16 if utilization >55% consistently.

Deliverables we promised: detailed per-month TCO workbook (sheet), per-token sensitivity curves, recommended SLA language draft, and a plan for hybrid on-prem fallback for most sensitive PII flows. Due: next_step deliverable (see next_step).
